published_prior_art.cite: BanKedagni2022 gives outer SDC bounds but no sharpness proof; KédagniLiMourifié2018 is non-archival WIP and does not supply accessible competing theorem text.
BanKedagni2022 Proposition 3.1 gives the normalized SDC outer union and explicitly states that sharpness is unproved.
KaidoMolinariStoye2019 and ChoRussell2024 treat projection or LP-value inference, not this SDC branch-disappearance family and set-risk lower bound.
KaidoMolinariStoye2019 provides asymptotic calibrated projection; the proposal's finite-sample Hoeffding whole-set projection is specific to the new exact-support map.
ChoRussell2024 and LevisEtAl2025 address generic LP-value or margin-based bound inference, not a completion-slack adaptation frontier for this discontinuous exact-set map.

source_verification_receipts.version: The Econometrics Journal 25(2), 477-493 (2022); open arXiv v1 corroboration at https://arxiv.org/html/2109.14785
source_verification_receipts.locator: Journal landing page, bibliographic record; corroborating arXiv v1 §2 Assumptions 2.1-2.3 and §3.1 Proposition 3.1, lines 71-78 and 184-195.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited paper studies BoS/SDC imperfect-IV bounds; its BoS condition is equality of factual and counterfactual conditional supports, Proposition 3.1 gives the SDC union, and the authors state that they lack a proof of sharpness.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform asymptotic coverage for calibrated projection under its regularity assumptions; it is not a finite-sample result for the proposed support-filtered union.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v10 (7 May 2023), corresponding to JBES 42(2), 563-578 (2024)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper bootstraps randomly perturbed linear-program value functions for uniformly valid inference on linear functionals or scalar subvectors of linearly moment-identified sets.

The paper gives margin-condition-based influence-function estimators of covariate-assisted Balke-Pearl bounds, with root-n behavior under stated nuisance-rate conditions; it does not claim the proposal's completion-slack frontier.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a generic strict-inclusion theorem identifying an observable class of laws on which the support filter strictly tightens Ban--Kédagni, beyond the single rational witness.
Develop the open question into a stated slack-indexed upper and lower rate frontier, with an explicit rate in kappa_n and a named adaptive construction.
Add a short LEI-specific strict example or explicitly frame the sharpness contribution as SDC-first, with LEI retained only as an extension pending a separate witness.

recommended_next_step: Advance the exact-support sharp-set kernel to Stage 0; retain the slack-adaptive inference question as a secondary, explicitly open extension.
